problems: Caption 'Everyone still went where they wanted to go' is not shown: across the whole storyboard the ten animals barely move apart. The knot near the yellow chicken stays in the same place, and only the left pig drifts in, along with small shuffles. Nobody visibly sets off toward a destination.

The rope does not act like a rope. In every frame the red lines are straight with no slack or sag, and no animal is ever pulled, dragged or held back by another (storyboard rows 2-4). Ten animals on one rope that never pull each other makes no physical sense, and nothing tells the viewer it is meant as a joke.

It reads as a branching star of red lines from a central knot, not as 'one rope' (caption). Some lines also run to the wooden swing frame at the top (at-50, at-75), so it is unclear what is tied to what.
Bodies overlap in the knot: the pigs, yellow chicken and blue bird push into each other at the lower left in at-50 and at-75, and the ropes go into bodies rather than attaching to them.
A stray brown stick floats next to the blue bird in the middle of the meadow (at-50 around the centre, at-75 above the blue bird), and nothing explains it.

The camera drifts and rotates the whole time while the animals hardly move, so the eye follows the camera move instead of any action. The animals are small in the frame, and the red mushroom and fence take up the foreground in rows 1-2.
posts.critique: The picture of ten animals joined by red lines is a nice idea, but the film never shows anyone going anywhere or the rope doing anything. The caption's punchline is therefore unsupported, and the rigid lines poking into a tangle of overlapping bodies look broken rather than funny.
